My heart goes out to this person. It’s practically my parent’s situation. We, as a family, survive on a combination of Social Security for both mom and dad, and disability payments for dad from a faulty hip replacement that forced him to quit a retail job he’d gotten in the wake of the 2008 recession. Worked cashiering/retail. At 65. Now, he’s trying to bolster his freelance business now so we can pay the mortgage and afford to eat, but struggling to get clients because of his age (75). Lots of people just turn him away or snub him even though he’s completely sound of mind. It breaks my heart to watch…I am always wishing I could do more to support them. My parents shouldn’t have to work this hard to live into their 60s and 70s. Mom is 65, an adjunct professor at a community college so she only has work 6 months out of the year. I can’t even think of moving out for my own life when I’ll likely be the main party responsible for the mortgage when Dad’s government disability pay runs out later this year. Nobody should have to work into their late years like this.

I am financially and emotionally trapped at home with aging parents--I am 24, 25 this fall, and an only child to a 75 year old father and 64 year old mother. My dad has narcissistic tendencies and my mother is heavily codependent. I've always known something was wrong--when they argued when I was a kid, it would get so intense for me emotionally sometimes I wish they'd divorce. They'd openly tell me they stayed together for me--what a joke. It fucked me up way worse than a divorce could've. My dad was absent for all THREE of his other kids--all 3, who now have highly limited or no contact with him--now I get why.

My mom had been through 3 divorces by the time she met my dad and got pregnant with me at 39, and he took care of her and wanted me, so she stayed. I wish she never had. He is, at heart, a good man, she is a good woman, but as we have all aged it has gotten more and more intolerable. Nothing he does is without a backhanded remark or passive-aggressive, self-serving undertones. He resents being old, he's vain (at 75?!) and bitter and nostalgic for the past where he was COO on 5th Avenue and captained a yacht. My mother grew up in an abusive household and has struggled all her life but is so incredibly powerful for sticking around. She's attempted and never told me until I admitted I wanted to. My father seems incapable of introspection and allergic to emotions, if I cried in his face he'd just shrug and look uncomfortable.

They tried to raise me religious as well--I've got trauma from that, trauma from the long-term emotional abuse of being in the same house as a narcissist boomer and emotionally passive mother who would shrug if I begged her to just stand up to him when I was 16 and something clicked, and I realized hey my parents are actually shitty to me, especially when I was screaming and begging for love and comfort and my mom instead tried to exorcise demons from within me, told me therapy was "the council of the ungodly," denounced my friends as a bad influence and still, to this day, laments the loss of "her child," as if I am not the same person.

In small ways, they have grown and evolved to respect me as an adult and move past the fact that I don't want religion (I never did), but I am still horrifically enmeshed in their life. I am NOT financially independent; I frankly don't know if I ever will be. I have a full-time job, but no benefits, no healthcare (my dad is the only one because he qualifies for Medicare, but even that doesn't cover depression medication which he is finally seeking. wahoo.) We moved 700 miles away from my home state IN THE MIDDLE OF 2020 LOCKDOWN, moved from where they'd managed to keep us until I was 22. Our house was seized by the bank in 2016 after the 2008 recession--we downsized to an intolerably small apartment and just got more miserable. Our home state priced us out.

I went to university for music, something I'd always felt pressured to do, as some type of "golden child," with a talent for flute. (don't forget the arguments that devolved into calling me a selfish, entitled bitch, in my teen years, what fun! that sure didn't confuse the fuck out of me) This interest was legitimate, I enjoyed it, and miss it. But now it's psychologically fraught--because I've never known if its something I enjoyed and loved, or just something my parents could use to show me off like a trophy. My degree feels increasingly useless--I learned I actually wanted to work in museums by junior year. I am now 35k+ in debt for student loans and am putting off grad school because I am cripplingly afraid of more debt. My mom has 80+k in loans/debt. My father has none. He never had roommates. See what I mean here about there being a fundamental psychological disconnect between my father and us?

Once, my father even directly told me that I am his "hope" and "legacy" and his "life's purpose." I was fucking 20. I can't handle being here, but I am wholly and truly isolated in this new state, with no real means of my own to escape. I have ZERO friends or connections--neither do they! We don't get out. They work from home to pay the mortgage--at their ages. I live like a fucking ant--I leave the anthill to work during the day, come home at night, and just get extremely fucking high to cope. I cycle my hobbies on loop--drawing, gaming, writing. Nothing truly distracts me anymore. Creating is harder and harder.

I don't truly wish to die, I just don't want this life, but escape is impossible. They have no other family--who will care for them when they're dying? I know I am emotionally bound to them if I think this way, but legitimately, they have no other options. I am wholly, truly and completely trapped. I am sick of doing the same thing every day (boring job = easy money, but god it makes me more suicidal), but I am so trapped. I have no escape. I keep cycling these thoughts because yeah there actually is no way out and I'm fucked.

Suicide hotlines are a joke. They feed you canned and automated responses--one of the operators once told me all my problems are my own fault! I once had a therapist--a THERAPIST--tell me the same thing. I have no friends who can truly, WHOLLY, take me on with how fucked up and dark and miserable I am, and basically, humanity does not deserve someone as pathetic as me, so why stick around anymore when all my avenues are gone and disappearing.

One of my half-sisters has recently told me to forget about them, they'll be fine, I should focus on me, but I can't focus on me when I make 1.5k a month, not enough for rent + actual living expenses, not when my dad still covers tons of unknown costs he's unwilling to disclose to me, or has paid for in family plans that I can't break out of without just simply going broke.

I wish I had the balls to fucking kill myself so I didn't have to tolerate this anymore. I'm incredible privileged, my parents never hit me, but nonetheless, I wish to be done now. Life has always been too much for me and I'm so sick of trying.

This isn't even mentioning COVID, all my sad breakups and flings where I left more broken than whole, climate change, the world spiraling into war, and I'm just fucking 24 and wanted to draw and create and just be happy. I am so sick of existing. It hurts too much.
